79741.subject: Team1 Thailand Is Here To Build
79741.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/team1-thailand-is-here-to-build

In Thailand, founders and developers often live ten minutes apart but never meet.
Team1 Thailand launches today to close that gap.
We are the Avalanche community layer for Thailand. We serve two crowds who rarely share a table: the digital nomads and international founders who cycle through Bangkok, Phuket, and Chiang Mai, and the local Thai developers and students who stand ready to code. Bringing these groups together will create one of Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing tech communities.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
Our track record so far:
Flagship events across the country, with our first ones in Chiang Mai, going beyond the usual Bangkok scene
A university workshop at Chulalongkorn, with the first hackathon there this week, and Kasetsart, Thammasat, KMITL, and MUIC to follow
Events co-hosted with 4 ecosystem partners: Pudgy Penguins, Binance TH, ST Thailand, and 4SEAS
Builders onboarded in both Thai and English, from first wallet to first deployment
Walk In And Start Building
Team1 Thailand is a group of people who show up for each other and for new people walking through the door. You see it in what people do before anyone hands them a task.
One member joined four months ago and has already run six events. Between them, he built an event badge mint on Avalanche C-Chain, so attendees leave with proof of attendance. Another arrived weeks ago and, without being asked, built a workshop on policy-gated AI agents, shipped a working repo, and deployed real contracts on Fuji, then carried it to a campus herself. A student pitched a monthly program at Thammasat before anyone suggested one. Someone else designed the first chapter merch.
No queue, no job description. People show up, build, and ship.
Built in Bangkok, Running Across Asia
Last May, we ran a padel night with the Pudgy Penguins APAC team. We had a small budget and no official status yet. But it worked, so it traveled: the Philippines, then Japan, then Taiwan.
A relationship that started in Bangkok now runs across the region. That is what a local team is for: close enough to the ground to spot the opening, and connected enough to take it everywhere.
The Banks Got There First
While other ecosystems focused on turnout, real infrastructure went live in Thailand. In December, Kasikornbank announced Seamless Travel Payments on Chain with Orbix Technology and StraitsX at the Singapore FinTech Festival, part of Project BLOOM under the Monetary Authority of Singapore. A Thai tourist in Singapore pays with Q-money from a KBank wallet; it converts to XSGD, and the merchant receives Singapore dollars in real time.
